sample_unit: observations (10 cases x 3 input conditions x 3 LLMs)

links.outcome: Self-reported diagnostic confidence of LLMs as textual input was enriched, without reference-standard benchmarking
links.effect: Self-reported confidence increased significantly with richer input (Friedman χ²=18.86; P<0.001; cumulative OR 5.43, 95% CI 3.00-9.81), possibly reflecting expressed certainty rather than improved reasoning.
links.quote: This pattern may reflect the tendency of an LLM to express greater certainty when given richer input rather than genuinely improved diagnostic reasoning.

links.outcome: Variation of LLM outputs (severity, confidence, detail) under varied input richness
links.effect: Severity scores did not differ among LLMs (χ²=2.31; P=0.31), but confidence rose with enriched input and reporting verbosity varied by model (P<0.001; Claude 5.67 vs ChatGPT 0.00 additional structures).
links.quote: Substantial variability in reporting behavior exists across models, particularly in output detail.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic confidence and reporting behavior of multiple LLMs when provided with varying levels of structured textual descriptions of salivary gland imaging, but it does not test a specific clinical deployment practice or safeguard.
